chunks: With this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever recites the Surah 'Nun wal-Qalam' in an obligatory or recommended prayer, Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, will keep him safe from poverty forever, and Allah will protect him from the squeeze of the grave when he dies.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah al-Qalam in prayer?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking the recitation of Surah al-Qalam to both material stability and spiritual comfort in the barzakh. This tradition highlights the Surah's unique capacity to ward off poverty (faq'r) and the constriction of the grave (damm al-qabr), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between worldly sustenance and hereafter rewards through specific Quranic recitations.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam as-Sadiq (a.s.) says: Whoever recites Surah “Noon wal  Qalam”  in  his  obligatory  or  recommended  prayers, Allah  would  always  keep  him  safe  and  protected  from destitution  and  poverty,  and  when  that  man  dies,  Allah would grant him exemption from the squeeze of the grave.
